# Guide for the last model-review round

Use a fresh conversation for each reviewer. For the first assessment, supply the individual essay PDF and the neutral request below. Keep earlier verdicts and this package's candidate ranking out of that first assessment. Afterward, use the focused questions to probe anything the initial review missed. This is a suggested procedure, not a record of reviews already completed.

## Neutral review request

Please give a fair, demanding review of the attached philosophy essay. Reconstruct its actual claim and the strongest defensible argument before criticizing it. Prioritize correctness, originality and philosophical importance. Distinguish a demonstrated error from an unresolved concern, and a useful special case from a new general result. Check the closest primary literature when accessible; identify precisely what you could not read. For each serious criticism, give the relevant passage, why the inference fails or remains unsupported, and what would repair it. Do not infer originality from formalism, numerical novelty or the absence of a remembered precedent. Do not assume the essay is defective merely because a broader result exists. Finish by stating what survives the criticism and whether its remaining contribution is worth reading. Do not rewrite the essay until the assessment is complete.

## Focused follow-up: A5

Does the distinction between unrestricted holism and marginal extensionality fairly capture Dorst's published argument? Does the counterexample satisfy the assumptions it actually challenges? Is Non-vacuity enough for the claimed rationality conclusion? Check the optimizer characterization, the sufficient refinement theorem and its limits. Given that *Good Guesses* reproduces the two principal belief sets, explain exactly what remains original and whether it matters philosophically.

Useful sources: Dorst 2019, §4.2 and Propositions 4–5; Dorst and Mandelkern, *Good Guesses*, especially the scoring rule, Filtering and belief application. The essay's section locators for the latter use the July 2021 penultimate draft.

## Focused follow-up: A6

Is the mapping to Value, Weak Value and Total Trust correct, including the fixed tie order? What does the gappedness characterization add to *Deference Done Better*, Theorem 4.1? Check finite versus continuous scope, availability of the questions, the future policy, and the conditional-rule examples. Does the costly-inquiry argument establish the claimed conflict with Conditional Knowledge Dominance? Distinguish the ordinary probability of weight-belief loss from its knowledge-conditional probability and from loss with a consistent discovery. Assess whether the remaining conclusion is philosophically important despite the stated escape routes.

Useful sources: Goodman and Salow, *Epistemology Normalized* and *Belief Revision Normalized*; Salow, *Fallibility and Dogmatism*; Dorst et al., [Deference Done Better](https://fitelson.org/ddb.pdf), Theorems 2.2 and 4.1 and Appendix B.

## Focused follow-up: A4

Are the witness-profile identities and cross-definition obstruction correct? Are anonymity, event coding and the Pareto condition motivated enough to make the result philosophically consequential? Compare the increment directly with Halpern and Wysocki rather than treating any normality counterexample as new. Check the fixed-context conformity lemma and its conditional application to Xiao and Xiong. The regularity-theory discussion in §7 has author-computed results but no separate implementation in this finishing pass; inspect those claims if they affect your verdict.

Useful sources: Halpern, *Actual Causality* (2016), especially the normality, preemption and conservative-extension discussions; Wysocki, [Conjoined Cases](https://simonstephan31.github.io/mec_dep_website/publications/wysocki_2023_conjoinedCases.pdf); Gallow 2021, pp. 85–86; Xiao and Xiong 2026, Definitions 12–13.

## Handling the responses

Preserve the essay version and model/version information with each review. Separate demonstrated errors, close prior-art matches, defensible disagreements and unsupported suspicions. Resolve substantive findings before changing prose; do not make revisions merely to satisfy every model's stylistic preference. Any substantive change should update the matching production report and word count. Reviewers' numerical grades are optional judgments, not evidence of correctness or novelty.
